entry.problem: Three distinct general failure mechanisms were identified from .autosaddler/training_evidence.json and the delivered trajectories. (1) vuls-ad2edbb8448e2c41a097f1c0b52696c0f6c5924d (0/7): the agent used ~45 tools (reads/greps/shell) but made zero file edits, then stopped with a summary; the outer harness 'Continue...' steer arrived after the loop had already exited, so no more model turns ran. Cause: the core loop exits at the first assistant stop in an idle state; there is no in-loop mechanism to detect 'used tools but implemented nothing' and continue. (2) ansible-935528e22e5283ee3f63a8772830d3d01f55ed8c (3/18): the agent edited source but verified only against stale pre-existing tests it had itself run/modified, believing work was complete; 15 required tests failed. Cause: no signal in tool output telling the agent that modifying or trusting local tests does not satisfy validation against pristine tests. (3) element-hq__element-web-5dfde12c1c1c0b6e48f17e3405468593e39d9492 (54/61): the agent edited test files and a shared test helper test/voice-broadcast/utils/test-utils.ts to make its local validation pass, contaminating 7 required tests that then failed under pristine tests. Same root cause as (2). All three are general capability gaps (no task-specific constants), addressed in core source: a zero-progress steer in the session loop and a test-file warning on file-editing tool outputs.

entry.problem: The declined candidate 7a088d22 (score 0.625 -> 0.625 vs parent beefdebd) failed because its zero-progress steer mutated the in-memory lastUserMsg.parts array and then continued the run loop; the loop reloads messages from the database every iteration (prompt.ts runLoop, MessageV2.filterCompactedEffect), so the steer text was never persisted and never reached the model. Root cause confirmed from the declined diff plus loop mechanics. The new patch persists a brand-new durable SessionV1.User message (fresh MessageID.ascending, agent/model copied from lastUser, valid minimal User schema shape) plus a synthetic SessionV1.TextPart via sessions.updateMessage/updatePart, logs 'zero-progress steer', and continues the loop; the next iteration reloads history from the DB, the exit condition lastAssistant.parentID === lastUser.id fails (lastUser is now the steer message), the model is called with the steer in history, and the resulting assistant message is created with parentID of the steer message so the loop exits normally. Steer conditions: finish === 'stop', no session.parentID (not subagent), agent !== 'plan', has tool parts, no completed edit/write/apply_patch/multiedit part, and a per-session cap of 2 escalating steers (module-level Map). Component B (unchanged from declined patch, whose mechanism was sound since tool outputs persist and reach the model): edit/write/apply_patch append TEST_FILE_WARNING to the persisted tool output when the target path matches test-directory or test-filename patterns (test-file-hint.ts), plus Effect.logInfo('test-file warning appended') as an observable engagement signal. All changes are general: no task IDs, no task-specific constants, no test data.

entry.problem: Training evidence shows both failed development cases failed because the agent modified the project's pristine test artifacts, and final validation runs the original tests, so such modifications are discarded and merely waste turns or mask real failures (vuls-4b680b99: snapshot regeneration via `yarn test -u`; element-web-44b98896: direct edits to existing test files). The previously accepted warning-only mechanism (TEST_FILE_WARNING appended after edits) was observed to be insufficient: the agent still proceeded to modify test artifacts after the warning. A scan of all 8 train cases found no case that required creating new test files and none that required modifying existing ones, so blocking only modification/deletion of existing test artifacts is safe. Hypothesis (not yet demonstrated on eval): hard errors at the tool-call boundary redirect the frozen target model to fix source files instead, converting contaminated trajectories into passing ones or at least saving wasted turns; the warning is retained for new-file creation which was never needed but stays permissive to avoid regressions.

assessment.evidence: Supporting: (1) matched before/after scores show vuls-4b680b99 improved 0.0 -> 1.0 under candidate 746b78ff while all 7 other matched cases were unchanged (aggregate 0.75 -> 0.875, strict matched-valid improvement accepted by the minibatch gate); (2) static code-route inspection of the accepted diff proves the guards are installed on every tool mutation path (edit.ts, write.ts, apply_patch.ts non-add changes, shell.ts command pre-check including snapshot-update flags). Against/limiting: (a) no run traces, logs, or tool-call records exist in the delivered evidence, so there is no observation of the guard actually firing or of the agent redirecting to source fixes; (b) element-web-44b98896, whose diagnosed failure mode the guard directly targets, remained failed, so engagement is un demonstrated there; (c) the patch is multi-component and a single-case flip cannot separate the guard effect from run-to-run variability. Conclusion: plausible but unproven.
assessment.next_step: Before stacking further changes on candidate 746b78ff, obtain trace- or tool-call-level evidence that the guard actually fires and that the agent subsequently edits source files: instrument the candidate (e.g. structured log of testFileBlockedMessage/shellTestArtifactGuard firings plus the next tool call after each block) and inspect the element-web-44b98896 trajectory specifically, since its failure mode is directly targeted yet the score did not change - distinguishing 'guard never fired' from 'fired but case fails anyway' decides whether to extend the guard or pursue a different mechanism.

entry.problem: Training evidence shows near-miss failures where the agent edits source files and then stops without completing verification: element-web-1077729a (385/386) and NodeBB-8168c6c4 (309/311) fail with single remaining unmet tests, and ansible-9a21e24 (11/14) similar. In these cases the session ends in an incomplete state, not from lack of edits (the accepted zero-progress steer in the parent only fires when no completed file edit exists) and not necessarily with an observed failing test run (the declined 564b4e5d failing-tests steer required a prior test command reporting failures, and was declined for insufficient mechanism evidence, so it is absent from parent). The uncovered behavioral gap is: the agent completes file edits, performs no shell/validation command after the last edit, and stops, claiming success without command-level verification. Hypothesis mechanism (to be validated by minibatch outcome): persisting a concrete, durable steer at that exact stop boundary re-engages the loop and causes a test run that either confirms the change or exposes the remaining failure to fix, converting near-miss stops into passes. The steer is delivered through the demonstrated-durable fa214efe mechanism (sessions.updateMessage/updatePart) that the loop reloads from the database each iteration, avoiding the non-engagement failure mode of declined 7a088d22 (in-memory-only steer). Risk bounded: fires at most once per session, only when a completed file edit exists, only when no completed bash run follows it, and only for finish=stop non-plan top-level sessions.
